**Adama City Football Club** ([Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"): _Garee Kubbaa Miilaa Magaalaa Adaamaa_ ; [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic "Amharic"): አዳማ ከተማ እግር ኳስ ክለብ) is an Ethiopian professional football club based in [Adama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama "Adama"), [Oromia Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromia_Region "Oromia Region"). The club was founded in 1991 and currently competes in the [Ethiopian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Premier_League "Ethiopian Premier League"), the top division of Ethiopian football.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-1) Adama City has a consistent appearance in the league except the one year where the team went to relegation. Best times are when the team finishing second in 2008 and staying on top of the league on 2017–18 for a while which ended at being 5th. The women team have won the title on 2018–19 with [Loza Abera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loza_Abera "Loza Abera") and [Senaf Wakuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senaf_Wakuma "Senaf Wakuma") winning the golden ball and boot respectively.
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adama_City_FC&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
The club was founded in 1991 (1983 [E.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_calendar "Ethiopian calendar")) by a group of local businessmen and athletes. Adama City quickly rose through the Ethiopian football pyramid, and in 2007 they were promoted to the Ethiopian Premier League for the first time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-:0-2)
The club has had a mixed record in the Ethiopian Premier League, but they have consistently been one of the top teams in the country. In [2017–18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Ethiopian_Premier_League "2017–18 Ethiopian Premier League"), Adama City briefly held the top spot in the league table, but they eventually finished in fifth place. In August 2018, the club hired Sisay Abraham as manager and Dawit Tadesse as assistant coach. The duo led Adama City to a fifth-place finish in the [2018–19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ethiopian_Premier_League "2018–19 Ethiopian Premier League") season.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-3)
In February 2021, the club hired Zaray Mulu as its manager. Mulu is a former player of the club, and he has previously managed other Ethiopian clubs, including [Hawassa City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawassa_City_S.C. "Hawassa City S.C.") and [Dedebit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedebit_F.C. "Dedebit F.C.").
Adama City is a popular club in Ethiopia with a large fan base. The club's home stadium is the [Adama Science and Technology University Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_Science_and_Technology_University "Adama Science and Technology University"), which has a capacity of 12,000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-5)
## Stadium
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adama_City_FC&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Stadium")]
The club's home ground is Adama Science and Technology University Stadium (Adama).
## Support
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adama_City_FC&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Support")]
Adama City (Ketema) enjoys a great support for its fans both at home in Adama and during away fixtures. The supporters have been involved in some altercation with some rival team supporters in the past.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-6)
## Finances
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adama_City_FC&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Finances")]
As of 2018, Salaries at the club have steadily risen with player like Jecko Peaze Peryze earning 165,000 Br per month.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-7) United Beverages, makers of the Ethiopian beer brand Anbessa Beer, is a sponsor of the club and in 2021 provided the club with new [Jako](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jako "Jako") branded Kits.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-:2-8)
### Sponsors
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adama_City_FC&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Sponsors")]
On March 25, 2022, Adama City football Club signed a sponsorship agreement with United Beverage for 60 million birr for 5 years.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adama_City_FC#cite_note-9)
